title: Chained tool orchestration: provenance-tagged result injection, streaming-safe guards, and back-compat layer
creator: Ava Chen
description: Enable robust multi-tool chaining inside the Core API while preserving structured outputs and streaming semantics. Deliver a small compatibility shim so older SDKs/users receive predictable behavior. Primary concerns: safe injection of tool results into downstream prompts with provenance metadata, preventing accidental recursion or runaway loops when tools re-invoke the runner, and ensuring streaming responses can be emitted incrementally without leaking intermediate tool state. Scope includes design docs, a compatibility adapter, runtime hooks for provenance tagging, soft/hard recursion limits, and end-to-end tests with synthetic and customer-like prompts.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: aligned on goals with PM and Product. Agreed we must attach opaque provenance tokens to any injected tool result (not raw tool outputs) and record a minimal provenance trail in traces and event logs.

2026-02-18 - Design sync notes: Decided on two-tier guard approach: soft guard (policy-based abort/warn and backoff) and hard guard (absolute loop counter per request + global per-session token TTL). Soft guard will surface in console as a warning and emit a metric 'tool.chain.soft_block'.

2026-02-23 - Prototype completed: implemented provenance tags as base64-encoded JSON blob containing {tool_key, timestamp, signature_version}. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8912

2026-03-02 - Review feedback from Security: remove plaintext tool outputs from non-authorized logs and ensure provenance blob uses HMAC-256 keyed by service API key. Security review ticket created: SEC-204.

2026-03-05 - Performance test: measured 95th percentile latency impact of injection metadata at 1.8% on synthetic streaming workload (seq len 512, batch 4). Found KV-cache miss rate increased slightly because injected tokens often have unique prefixes; mitigation: provide an option to inject summarized sentinel instead of full content for caching-friendly paths.

2026-03-10 - UX/SDK discussion: Need a compatibility shim for older SDKs that expect plain text tool results in the final stream. Plan: default behavior emits structured tool objects on new API; compatibility adapter collapses structured tool result into a single 'assistant' message while preserving provenance in X-Response-Meta header.
2026-03-12 - PR opened for runtime changes and compatibility shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9034. Tests added for recursion ceilings and backoff policies.
decisions: Provenance tokens: use compact base64 HMAC'ed blobs with versioning (v1). Visible only to telemetry and authorized debug APIs; not shown to end-user by default.
Guards: implement soft policy (configurable per-route) + hard counter (default 5 tool re-invocations per request). Hard counter enforced at service layer to avoid runaway CPU usage.

Streaming: allow incremental emission of tool 'meta' frames (tool-start, tool-progress, tool-end) in new structured protocol; compatibility layer will synthesize a single textual replacement for older clients.
Compatibility: default API v2 will return structured tool outputs. Add X-Compat-Version request header handling to enable legacy behavior for SDKs older than 2025-12.
Logging: redact raw tool outputs from system logs unless request has debug flag and owner consent. Metricize redaction events.
next_steps: Finalize PR feedback and address Security comments (SEC-204). Estimate 2 days for fixes and re-review.
Implement sentinel-based injection mode and add benchmark for KV cache hit improvement.
Add e2e test harness with a simulated customer chain that calls 3 different tools and attempts recursive invocation to validate hard guard.
Ship compatibility shim in SDKs after runtime change lands; coordinate with SDK team for a small minor release and migration notes.
Prepare console dashboard: add 'Tool Chain Events' view and alert on 'tool.chain.hard_block' > 0.
